hypotheses.description: Independent candidate explanations, ordered by likelihood. Produce at least two genuinely different ones — the point of this exercise is breadth, not confirming the first idea. Do not include variations of a single theory dressed up as alternatives.

theory.description: One sentence naming the root cause.

mechanism.description: The precise causal chain from root cause to observed symptom. Name real files, functions, and lines you actually read. A mechanism you cannot trace concretely is a guess — mark its confidence low.

evidence_for.description: Observations from the codebase or the symptom report that this theory explains.

evidence_against.description: Observations this theory fails to explain, or facts that argue against it. Be rigorous here — a hypothesis with no listed counter-evidence usually means you did not look.

discriminating_test.description: A concrete check whose outcome distinguishes THIS theory from the others. 'Add logging and see' is not discriminating. State what result would confirm and what would refute.

most_likely.description: Which hypothesis you would bet on, and why it beats the runner-up specifically.

cheapest_decisive_test.description: The single fastest check that eliminates the largest number of hypotheses at once. Prefer one that splits the space roughly in half over one that confirms your favourite.

ruled_out.description: Explanations you considered and eliminated, with the reason. Prevents the next investigator re-treading them.

missing_evidence.description: What you would need to see — a log, a repro, a value at runtime — to make real progress. Empty if the report was sufficient.
